findings.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:117 — `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` accesses `.integration` without optional chaining; when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null/empty, any booking with Google Meet location throws TypeError in the core booking path

[High/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (deleteEvent ~line 314, updateEvent ~line 255) — fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so find compares against undefined and always returns undefined; delete/update without externalCalendarId get `calendarId === undefined` and fail (the `find(...)?.externalId` pattern is also a no-op)

[Medium/bug] packages/lib/CalendarService.ts, office365calendar, larkcalendar — services still operate only on `destinationCalendar[0]` and ignore which credential invokes createEvent, so collective bookings with multiple hosts on the same provider create duplicate events in the first host's calendar and none in the others; only Google matches by credentialId

[Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1085 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently drops all team destination calendars when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, so collective events where only non-organizer hosts have destination calendars create no calendar events at all; should coalesce to `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` before pushing

[Medium/data] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1874 — booking record only connects `destinationCalendar[0]`, so downstream flows rebuilding evt from booking.destinationCalendar (paypal-webhook.ts, webhook.ts, confirm.handler, etc.) only see the first host's calendar, regressing collective paid/confirmed bookings to single-destination

[Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts (createAllCalendarEvents else-branch) — `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the new externalId argument, so result.externalId is undefined and booking references store no externalCalendarId; later reschedule/cancel of such bookings can't target the right calendar

[Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts (updateCalendarReferences loop) — if a reference's credentialId matches neither this.calendarCredentials nor a DB record, credential stays undefined and `updateEvent(credential, ...)` throws TypeError inside updateEvent; the broad try/catch converts all calendar references to failure results, so one broken reference fails every calendar update for the booking

[Medium/data] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts (loadUsers) — dynamic-event branch (prisma.user.findMany) dropped `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the select, so downstream logic reading user.organization sees undefined for dynamic collective bookings

[Medium/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:148-152 — slug logic was inverted: previously slug was set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false (and requestedSlug when true); now slug is set when billing is enabled, changing organization-creation behavior unrelated to the PR's purpose

[Low/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~156 — `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` silently creates the event in the user's primary calendar when no destination entry matches credentialId, potentially creating unexpected events in the wrong calendar during the migration window

[Low/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (createEvent/updateEvent) — the "main host" organizer attendee email is always taken from destinationCalendar[0] regardless of which credential creates the event, so events in other hosts' calendars show the first host's calendar email as organizer

[Medium/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts — the only test change is updating the expected destinationCalendar shape to []; there is no test coverage for the new collective multi-destination behavior (multiple hosts' calendars created, per-credential matching, update/delete of all references) across create/update/cancel/reschedule paths

[Low/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts (~line 425) — DB fallback prisma.credential.findUnique omits the app include used elsewhere (EventManager's fetch includes app.slug); getCalendar implementations relying on appId/app metadata may misbehave for credentials not present in bookingToDelete.user.credentials

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (deleteEvent ~line 314, updateEvent ~line 255) — fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so find compares against undefined and always returns undefined; delete/update without externalCalendarId get `calendarId === undefined` and fail (the `find(...)?.externalId` pattern is also a no-op)

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent, the fallback branch is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. That `find(...)` is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/falsy, making the lookup effectively always return `undefined`. This means the intended fallback to a destination calendar externalId does not work (and may result in `calendarId` being undefined or defaulting incorrectly).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/lib/CalendarService.ts, office365calendar, larkcalendar — services still operate only on `destinationCalendar[0]` and ignore which credential invokes createEvent, so collective bookings with multiple hosts on the same provider create duplicate events in the first host's calendar and none in the others; only Google matches by credentialId

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `Calendar.createEvent` to accept `(event, credentialId)`. `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent` once per destination/credential, but most non-Google implementations still select the calendar using only the first destination: e.g. `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` and `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` do `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`. `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` similarly filters calendars based on `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`. This means when multiple destination calendars exist (e.g. COLLECTIVE pushes team members’ destination calendars), repeated createEvent calls will target `destinationCalendar[0]`, causing duplicates in the first calendar and none in the others. Only `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent` uses the passed `credentialId` to pick the matching destination calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1085 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently drops all team destination calendars when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, so collective events where only non-organizer hosts have destination calendars create no calendar events at all; should coalesce to `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` before pushing

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is explicitly set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null,`). Immediately after, for collective team events, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. Because of optional chaining, this push is a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, so team members’ destination calendars collected into `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently not added to the event. The finding’s core claim (silent drop unless you coalesce/initialize to an array) is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1874 — booking record only connects `destinationCalendar[0]`, so downstream flows rebuilding evt from booking.destinationCalendar (paypal-webhook.ts, webhook.ts, confirm.handler, etc.) only see the first host's calendar, regressing collective paid/confirmed bookings to single-destination

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, explicitly appends additional team members' destination calendars (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` in `handleNewBooking.ts`). However, when persisting the booking it only connects `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` (see `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`), so the booking record retains only the first destination calendar. Downstream flows shown in the diff (e.g., `paypal-webhook.ts`, `webhook.ts`, `confirm.handler.ts`, `editLocation.handler.ts`) rebuild `evt.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (singular) and wrap it into a one-element array, so they can only ever see/create/update against that first calendar, losing the additional COLLECTIVE destinations captured earlier in memory.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts (createAllCalendarEvents else-branch) — `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the new externalId argument, so result.externalId is undefined and booking references store no externalCalendarId; later reschedule/cancel of such bookings can't target the right calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when `destination.credentialId` is falsy the code still calls `createEvent(c, event)` (no `externalId` third arg) inside `Promise.all(destinationCalendarCredentials.map(...))`. After this diff, `CalendarManager.createEvent` returns `externalId` only from that optional argument, and `EventManager` now stores booking references using `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined`. Therefore this branch produces results with `externalId` undefined, so references won’t persist `externalCalendarId`, which can break later update/delete targeting by external calendar id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~156 — `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` silently creates the event in the user's primary calendar when no destination entry matches credentialId, potentially creating unexpected events in the wrong calendar during the migration window

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `selectedCalendar` is now derived via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId;`. If `destinationCalendar` is non-empty but none of its entries matches the passed `credentialId`, `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` and the insert call uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, which will create the event in the user's primary calendar instead of the intended destination calendar. This is a behavioral regression vs. the new intent (select by credentialId) and can cause events to be created in the wrong calendar without any error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (createEvent/updateEvent) — the "main host" organizer attendee email is always taken from destinationCalendar[0] regardless of which credential creates the event, so events in other hosts' calendars show the first host's calendar email as organizer

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `createEvent` and `updateEvent` now derive `mainHostDestinationCalendar` via array destructuring (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...`) and then set the organizer attendee `email` from that first element (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : organizer.email`). However, event creation selects the target calendar per-credential (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`) and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` iterates over multiple `destinationCalendar` entries, creating events for different credentials. This means events created for non-first destinations will still use destinationCalendar[0] for the organizer attendee email, matching the finding’s described mis-association.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts — the only test change is updating the expected destinationCalendar shape to []; there is no test coverage for the new collective multi-destination behavior (multiple hosts' calendars created, per-credential matching, update/delete of all references) across create/update/cancel/reschedule paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new multi-destination calendar behavior (e.g., `destinationCalendar` is now an array in types; `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over multiple destinations and fetches credentials from DB; update/cancel paths now process multiple `_calendar` references via `.filter(...)` and `for ... of` loops in `rescheduleBooking` and `handleCancelBooking`). However, the only visible test adjustment is in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts`, changing an expected `destinationCalendar` from `null` to `[]`, with no added tests asserting multi-host/collective calendar creation, per-credential externalId matching in Google (`createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)` selecting `destinationCalendar.find(cal.credentialId===credentialId)`), or multi-reference update/delete behavior. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a direct defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts (~line 425) — DB fallback prisma.credential.findUnique omits the app include used elsewhere (EventManager's fetch includes app.slug); getCalendar implementations relying on appId/app metadata may misbehave for credentials not present in bookingToDelete.user.credentials

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a DB fallback in handleCancelBooking.ts that calls prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } }) without including app/app.slug. However, in this file the returned credential is only passed to getCalendar(calendarCredential) and then used for deleteEvent; the diff shows no use of app.slug/appName/app metadata there. The comparison to EventManager’s include(app.slug) is not evidence of a defect here, because EventManager constructs a CredentialWithAppName object for createEvent, while handleCancelBooking appears to operate on raw Credential records (bookingToDelete.user.credentials also lacks app include). Any claim that getCalendar “relies on appId/app metadata” cannot be verified from this diff alone.
